housing: Crawley is a post-war new town, built in neighbourhoods each with its own shops, so most homes are 1950s to 1980s terraces, semis and low-rise flats, with a large council-owned stock. Gatwick Airport is a major employer and drives demand for private lets, including shared houses and rooms. The town centre has seen many office-to-flat conversions and new apartment blocks, and Forge Wood is the newest neighbourhood. Older Victorian homes survive mainly around Three Bridges and the old high street.
checkinTips: Former new town council houses: photograph gardens, fences, sheds, the boiler and the consumer unit.
Office-to-flat conversions in the town centre: check room sizes, window opening, ventilation and any condensation, and note fob and post box keys.
Shared houses let to airport workers: photograph each room's lock and furniture and the shared kitchen appliances separately.
Homes under the Gatwick flight path: note window and door seals and any secondary glazing.
New-build flats and houses at Forge Wood: record allocated parking, bin and bike stores and any snagging still open.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair or unsafe conditions in a private rented home can contact Crawley Borough Council's private sector housing team.
